extracted.intended_audience: educated American readers, reformers, policymakers, and students of political theory interested in the democratic promise of the United States
extracted.subtask_description: A political-theoretic exposition of what the 'Promise of American Life' means and the standards Americans must meet to realize it; addresses economic, political, moral, and social conditions required to fulfill democratic ideals. Intended as guidance for public thought and reform rather than a technical checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise must be determined by an ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: The only fruitful promise of which the life of any individual or any nation can be possessed, is a promise determined by an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nation's promise must be more than confident anticipation or mere pursuit of success; it must derive its value from a specific and worthy purpose (an ideal) that directs planning and action rather than passive expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulfillment requires deliberate, strenuous effort
rubrics_metrics.description: The better future ... must be planned and constructed rather than fulfilled of its own momentum; it must be fulfilled by laborious, single-minded, clear-sighted, and fearless work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating the national future as self-fulfilling destiny; implementation demands organized, sustained effort and willingness to plan and act intentionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Promise is a responsibility, not just prophecy
rubrics_metrics.description: From the point of view of an immigrant this Promise may consist of the anticipation of a better future ... but once he has become an American, the Promise can no longer remain merely an anticipation. It becomes ... a responsibility, which requires for its fulfillment a certain kind of behavior on the part of himself and his fellow-Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizenship entails obligations: individuals must behave in particular ways (civic, moral, economic) to make the Promise real; passivity or mere expectation is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to sacrifice traditional means to realize the ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: He must be prepared to sacrifice to that traditional vision even the traditional American ways of realizing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fidelity to the national tradition does not mean rigid adherence to past practices; fulfilling the democratic ideal may require abandoning familiar institutions or methods when they obstruct progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic independence and widely accessible prosperity
rubrics_metrics.description: To the European immigrant ... the Promise of America has consisted largely in the opportunity which it offered of economic independence and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Promise concretely includes broad access to economic opportunity and independence; policy and social arrangements should preserve and expand such access rather than allow its restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free political institutions must accompany economic opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: This economic independence and prosperity has always been absolutely associated in the American mind with free political institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic gains alone are insufficient; they must be secured within a framework of political freedom and democratic institutions that protect and enable popular access to opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy must produce moral and social benefits, not merely material wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: This economic and political system must be made to secure results of moral and social value. It is the seeking of such results which converts democracy from a political system into a constructive social ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate success not only by prosperity but by improvements in civic character, social amelioration, and moral development of the populace; institutions should be judged by these broader outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine individual effort with proper political organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The increasing comfort and economic independence of an ever increasing proportion of the population must be secured by a combination of individual effort and proper political organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and reform should balance incentives for personal initiative with collective political structures that distribute opportunity and guard against concentrations of power that obstruct mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent monopolization of opportunities; maintain equality of access
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the economic and political evils which are now becoming offensively obtrusive are directly or indirectly derived from the gradual monopolization of certain important economic opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard against the concentration or monopolization of economic opportunities through social, legal, or political means to preserve the 'broad equality of sentiment' rooted in equal material opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arouse the mass to activity by satisfying needs and sharpening expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The mass of mankind must be aroused to still greater activity by a still more abundant satisfaction of their needs, and by a consequent increase of their aggressive discontent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social policy should raise living standards in ways that stimulate popular initiative and constructive demand for further improvement, not induce complacency or resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic culture that discourages rigid social distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our democratic prohibition of any but occasional social distinctions and our democratic dislike to any suggestion of authentic social inferiority have contributed ... to the fluid and elastic substance of American life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve cultural and institutional norms that resist caste-like hierarchies and social inhibition, fostering fluidity and upward mobility as part of fulfilling the national Promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate methods with the ideal; reassess means as conditions change
rubrics_metrics.description: The fault ... does not consist in the expectation of some continuity of achievement. It consists rather in the expectation that the familiar benefits will continue to accumulate automatically. In his mind the ideal Promise is identified with the processes and conditions which hitherto have very much simplified its fulfillment, and he fails sufficiently to realize that the conditions and processes are one thing and the ideal Promise quite another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously evaluate whether existing institutions and processes still advance the democratic ideal; be ready to reform the means when social or economic conditions change.
